candidates.change_summary: Change the return value from ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector to a different bytes4 constant like 0x00000000.
Change the return value from ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector to a different bytes4 constant like 0xFFFFFFFF.
Make the function revert by adding a require(false) or revert() statement before the return, changing the behavior under the target condition from completing to reverting.
Delete the return statement so the function reverts or returns default zero value, which differs from the original selector.
Remove the assignment to baseToken so it retains its default zero address.
Replace the assignment to baseToken with a constant zero address assignment.
Replace the assignment of nft with a different address to cause the nft state variable to differ after initialization.
Replace the changeFee assignment to use a constant zero instead of the parameter _changeFee.
Delete the statement that assigns changeFee = _changeFee, so changeFee remains its default value.
Replace the changeFee assignment to add one to the parameter _changeFee.
Replace the fee rate input validation require/revert with a higher threshold; instead of reverting when > 5000, revert when > 10000, which allows a different feeRate to be stored.
Delete the fee rate validation check entirely, so any _feeRate (even > 5000) can be stored.
Remove the `if (initialized) revert AlreadyInitialized();` check so initialize can be called again, overwriting `feeRate` to a different value on subsequent calls.
Assign a constant 0 to feeRate instead of the parameter `_feeRate`, so the stored feeRate is always different.
Assign the parameter `_baseToken` (cast to uint16) to feeRate instead of `_feeRate`, storing a completely different value.
